_source: AI-researched venue CANDIDATES for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly edited by the research agent. Populated by a daily scheduled research agent (2026-08, at explicit user request: 'fan out some research agents who's goal is to run every day to find and suggest new businesses... they shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet'; bumped from ~3-5/day to 10/day at a later explicit request). See .claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md for the full research brief/rules this agent works under (Hard rule 1 chain/fast-food screening, real coordinates only, no duplicates, Do/Drink/Eat coverage balance). The research agent commits straight to master for this file (no PR — this queue has zero effect on the live app, nothing reads it except the review agent and the admin dashboard's Growth Insights context). A second, independent daily agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) re-verifies each `pending` entry and is the only thing that ever promotes one into the real docs/data/venues.json, behind its own pull request — see that file's own doc comment for why the human checkpoint lives there instead of here. Each entry mirrors docs/data/venues.json's own raw shape (name/district/type/spend/lat/lon/base/bands/reason) exactly, so a reviewed-and-approved entry can be moved into that file with a straight copy-paste, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) that get stripped on promotion. `district` values must be a real existing district id from docs/data/districts.json (manchester/cheshire metros only) UNLESS the entry is itself proposing a brand-new district — see district-suggestions.json for that case instead; a venue suggestion should never invent a district id that doesn't exist anywhere.
_reviewWorkflow: status starts 'pending' on every new entry. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent changes it to 'approved' (then copies the venue fields into docs/data/venues.json and removes the entry here, as part of its own PR) or 'rejected' (left here with researchNotes explaining why, as a record so the same candidate isn't re-suggested later — curia-research-daily checks every entry here regardless of status before suggesting anything new). A human's actual review happens by reading/merging the review agent's PR, not by editing this file directly, though a human reviewer (or a future admin-dashboard screen) can still hand-edit an entry's status here if needed.

suggestions.name: The Yard
suggestions.reason: A greengrocer, a bakery and a juice bar built round a shared courtyard since 2012 — market-hall energy squeezed onto a converted Cheshire builder's plot.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED 2026-09-02 by curia-suggestion-review, independent re-verification. The greengrocer/artisan-butchery/organic-bakery/juice-bar retail concept this entry describes closed back in February 2017 (alderleyedge.com, 'The times they are a-changin as The Yard closes cafe and shop' — owners cited high rent and restructured). Since then the South Street site has operated as a private events/function-hire space only (gigs, workshops, parties, the 'Yard Sessions' concert series) — no evidence found of the retail/cafe side reopening, in 2026 or otherwise. The original researchNotes' 2013-era sources (Hungry Hoss, goodfoodshops.blogspot) predate the 2017 closure and no longer describe current reality. Do not re-suggest under this market-hall/greengrocer framing; an entry describing it accurately as an events/function space could be reconsidered separately.

suggestions.name: ATOMECA Wine Bar
suggestions.reason: Schofield's own second act on The Avenue — a walk-in wine list built around small plates, not the cocktail menu working next door.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED 2026-09-02 by curia-suggestion-review, independent re-verification. ATOMECA is not a single site: the original opened at Deansgate Square, Owen Street, in 2021, and this Spinningfields/The Avenue site is a second location of the identical brand ('Schofields and Brandwood to launch second Atomeca' — classbarmag.com; also confirmed via spinningfields.co.uk's own news post and a Manchester's Finest listing describing it as following 'the success of the first ATOMECA at Deansgate Square'). This is a different situation from this file's accepted Craig's/Ivy Spinningfields or Cibo/Suburban Green precedent, where the same owners run two venues under two distinct names/concepts — here the same brand name is simply repeated at a second address, which reads as a small chain under Hard rule 1, not a single independent venue. Do not re-suggest either ATOMECA location.

suggestions.name: Clark Art
suggestions.reason: Bill Clark's own gallery on Ashley Road since 1999, deep in L.S. Lowry and the northern painters he's written the books on — a private dealer's eye, not a gallery chain's algorithm.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED 2026-09-02 by curia-suggestion-review, independent re-verification. Clark Art permanently closed on Thursday 3 October 2024, when owner Bill Clark retired after 18 years trading at 155 Ashley Road, Hale ('An incredible journey: Clark Art to close after 18 years in Hale village' — altrincham.todaynews.co.uk). The gallery no longer exists; the original researchNotes' sources (artsy.net, halebarns.com, an Antiques Trade Gazette profile) are all pre-closure and don't reflect this. Do not re-suggest.
